div.head: II Cn 66
div.ab: Gif hwa Godes flyman hæbbe on unriht, agyfe hine to rihte ⁊ forgilde þam þe hit gebyrige; ⁊ gylde þam cingce be (his) weregylde.
Be Godes flyman. Gyf hwa Godes flyman hæbbe on unriht, agyfe hine mid rihte ⁊ forgylde ðam ðe hit gebyrige; ⁊ gylde ðam kynincge be wergilde.
Gif hwa Godes fliman hæbbe on unriht, agife hine to rihte ⁊ forgylde þam þe hit gebyrige; ⁊ gylde þam cyninge hine be weregilde.
Si quis Dei fugitiuum habeat iniuste, reddat eum ad rectum et persoluat ei cui ius erit; et regi emendet secundum wéregildum.
Si quis Godes flyman iniuste habuerit, reddat eum ad iusticiam et persoluat despectum cui iustum est; et regi emendet pretium, id est be þere.
Si quis autem Dei commodum tenet contra ius, reddat et persoluat ei cui oportet; regi autem persoluat suam redempcionem.
Be Godes flyman. Gyf hwa Godes flyman hæbbe on unriht, agyfe hine mid rihte ⁊ forgylde ðam ðe hit gebyrige, ⁊ gylde ðam kynincge be wergilde.
Gif hwa Godes flyman hæbbe on unriht, agyfe hine to rihte and forgilde þam þe hit gebyrige, and gylde þam cingce be his weregylde.

(Über den vom Kirchen-Gericht Geächteten. B) Wenn einer einen [dem Rechtsanspruch] der Kirche Entflohenen [Geächteten] unrechtmässig bei sich hat, so liefere er ihn zum Gerichte (gesetzlich B) aus und bezahle dem [Gerichtsherrn], dem es gebührt [für Beschützung Widerspänstiger Busse zu empfangen]; und zahle (ihn A falsch) dem König mit (seinem G) Wergeld.

(Concerning one outlawed by the church court. B) If anyone unlawfully keeps with him a fugitive from [the legal claim of] the Church [an outlaw], let him hand him over to the court (lawfully, B) and pay the [lord of the court] to whom it is due [to receive the fine for harbouring the recalcitrant]; and let him pay (him, A, wrongly) to the king with (his, G) wergild.

Concerning excommunicated persons. If anyone unlawfully maintains an excommunicated person, he shall deliver him up in accordance with the law, and pay compensation to him to whom it belongs, and to the king a sum equivalent to his wergeld.
If anyone wrongfully maintains God’s fugit ive, he is to give him up to justice and pay compensation to whom it belongs; and he is to pay to the king the amount of the wergild.
If anyone illegally shelters an excommunicated person, he shall surrender him to the lawful authorities and pay compensation to whom it belongs, and pay his wergild to the king.
div.note: In A, ‘hine’ is written with the abbreviation ·N· and is missing in the other MSS; Liebermann thinks it not original. He also thinks G's ‘(his)’ probably not original.; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 353, October 2026 (MS Cons); AP: corrected against Whitelock p. 471, October 2026 (was “fugitive,”, now “fugit ive,”)

Used by Hn 11, 14. Owing to the unfinished state of the redaction, two sentences with partly the same premise but different consequences stand side by side, one in the words of the source, the other in Cnut’s; see above Introduction 18
Vgl. Gl Exkommunikation 15. a b; friedlos 2. Das Wort war um 1100 veraltet, da Inst es als nicht mehr verstanden unübersetzt lässt und C¹⁰ es falsch liest. Keineswegs ‘entflohenen Mönch’ (Price)
Cf. Gl Exkommunikation 15. a b; friedlos 2. The word was obsolete by c. 1100, since Inst leaves it untranslated as no longer understood, and C¹⁰ misreads it. By no means ‘runaway monk’ (Price)

note.label: ive
note.seg: Robertson translates “an excommunicated person”. If the same person is meant as in 66.1, the heavy penalty in that may imply a persistent refusal to surrender him. Alternatively, “God’s fugitive” could be one who fled rather than appear to answer the charge in an ecclesiastical process.
